name: Talkspace
one_liner: Online therapy with a licensed therapist by messaging and live video, billed weekly or through many insurance plans; psychiatry is a separate service.
best_for: Adults with depression, anxiety or stress who want a therapist they can message between live sessions
People whose insurance or employer plan covers Talkspace
People who would rather write to a therapist than keep fixed weekly appointments
not_for: Anyone in crisis: call or text 988
People who need controlled medications such as stimulants or benzodiazepines (Talkspace does not prescribe them)
People with severe mental illness who need intensive or in-person care
short_description: Online therapy by messaging and video with a licensed therapist; $69–$109/week self-pay, or a copay through many insurance plans.
long_description: Talkspace is a US online therapy service. After an intake you are matched with a licensed therapist and can message them at any time and, depending on your plan, have live video sessions. Talkspace's pricing page lists self-pay therapy at $69 to $99 a week depending on the plan, with a premium tier at $109 a week; quarterly or twice-yearly billing costs less, and many insurance and employer plans are accepted. Psychiatry (medication management) is billed separately: $299 for the first evaluation and $175 per follow-up without insurance, and Talkspace does not prescribe controlled substances. Three randomized trials run on the platform, published in 2023, 2024 and 2025, found that messaging-based therapy worked about as well as weekly video therapy for depression; most were co-authored by Talkspace researchers. Universal Health Services completed its purchase of Talkspace in August 2026.
patient_summary: You answer an intake questionnaire, get matched with a licensed therapist, then message them any time and meet by live video depending on your plan. Without insurance it costs $69–$109 a week; many insurance and employer plans cover it, so check coverage at sign-up. Medication is a separate psychiatry service, and controlled substances are not prescribed.

pricing.notes: Self-pay therapy plans run $69–$99/week, with a $109/week premium tier; quarterly or biannual billing saves about 10–20%. Couples therapy and psychiatry are priced separately (psychiatry $299 first visit, $175 follow-up). Many insurance and employer plans accepted; check coverage at sign-up.

privacy.notes: Talkspace's US state privacy notice says it discloses personal information to third parties for analytics and advertising (you can opt out), but says it does not sell, share or target ads once you are a patient using the portal; care records fall under its HIPAA notice. Chat history can be deleted on request; medical records are kept as the law requires.

faqs.a: Talkspace accepts many major insurance plans including Aetna, Cigna, Optum/UnitedHealthcare, Premera, and some Blue Cross plans. Many employers also offer Talkspace as an EAP benefit. Check the Talkspace website to verify your specific plan's coverage before signing up.

faqs.q: How much does Talkspace cost without insurance?
faqs.a: Without insurance, Talkspace therapy costs $69-109/week depending on the plan. Psychiatry for medication management costs $249 for the initial evaluation plus $125 for follow-up appointments. These are out-of-pocket costs if your insurance doesn't cover telehealth therapy.

Yes, Talkspace offers psychiatry services for medication management. Licensed psychiatrists and psychiatric nurse practitioners can prescribe non-controlled medications for anxiety, depression, and other conditions. Controlled substances (Adderall, benzodiazepines) have significant restrictions.

Talkspace advantages: accepts insurance, offers psychiatry. BetterHelp advantages: larger therapist network, slightly cheaper without insurance. If your insurance covers Talkspace, it's usually the better value. If paying cash, BetterHelp offers similar therapy at lower cost.

citation.title: Comparing Message-Based Psychotherapy to Once-Weekly, Video-Based Psychotherapy for Moderate Depression: Randomized Controlled Trial

clinical_trials.outcome: Message-based therapy was noninferior to weekly video therapy on depression, anxiety and functional impairment.

clinical_trials.outcome: No meaningful differences between messaging and video in depression, anxiety, disability or global improvement at 6 or 12 weeks.
